clues: I have travelled further than most adventurers.
I was not always the shape I am now.
You will find me wandering towns, never the same one for long.
A certain amulet lets you hear what I have to say.
Meow.
Kings and councils have argued within my walls for centuries.
I am the beating heart of Misthalin's trade.
A fountain, a museum and a palace stand within me.
The Grand Exchange lies just beyond my north-west gate.
Zaff, Aubury and Horvik all call me home.
I have been the mark of a seasoned warrior for more than two decades.
I come from a creature that only those trained to 85 Slayer may harm.
I am held in one hand, yet I cannot train Strength on my own.
A kraken's appendage can be bound to me, though I will eventually crumble to dust.
A coiled demonic spine that cracks through the air.
Countless adventurers have trained their strength with me at their side.
You must survive an island of hostile primates before you may wield me.
Daga sells me for 100,000 coins once you earn the right.
My special attack can sever an opponent's protection prayers.
The curved crimson blade of Ape Atoll.
Many wear me with pride, though some still tremble at the memory of earning me.
No coin can buy me; you must survive sixty-three waves to claim me.
I am forged in the volcanic heart of Karamja.
Defeating TzTok-Jad is the final trial before I drape across your shoulders.
Molten lava flows endlessly down my back.
In the old days, wearing me meant you had truly made it.
Free-to-play warriors still chase the quest required to put me on.
Oziach in Edgeville refuses to sell me until you prove your worth.
You must slay Elvarg on Crandor before my straps will fit you.
The brightest cyan chestpiece a free-to-play adventurer can wear.
I cost almost nothing, yet treasure hunters never leave home without me.
I turn earth for farmers and uncover graves for the brave.
Six crypts in Morytania only open their doors to my iron edge.
Wilderness player-killers have long been mocked for claiming me as loot.
Dig here.
I change hands millions of times a day without ever tiring.
No matter how many of me you gather, I take up only one slot.
My pile changes shape ten times as I grow from one to ten thousand.
A single stack of me stops growing at 2,147,483,647.
Gold pieces — the lifeblood of the Grand Exchange.
I look humble and battered, yet I have saved more lives than most gilded armour.
I am handed out freely to those brave enough to face a winged terror.
Duke Horacio keeps a supply of me upstairs in Lumbridge Castle.
Attach a draconic visage to me and I become something far mightier.
Without me, a single breath of dragonfire will roast you alive.
I am one of the first tools placed into a newcomer's hands.
I am useless alone, yet paired with wood I light the way.
Those who have trained with Otto can leave me behind, though most still carry me.
Every Wintertodt brazier and campfire across Gielinor owes its spark to me.
Strike flint and steel: logs become ashes.
I am the reward at the end of a very long feast.
Despite my name, I have nothing to do with Morytania's six brothers.
You need 175 Quest Points and a defeated Culinaromancer to unlock me.
A chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar sells me for 130,000 coins.
The iconic brown handwear at the climax of Recipe for Disaster.
I begin my life as a humble branch cut beneath watchful spirits.
You must carve me yourself on an island where weapons are forbidden.
I am the key to a hidden market upon Gielinor's moon.
Complete the Lumbridge and Draynor Elite Diary and you may finally bank me for good.
Hold me in hand to step through a fairy ring.
Three hidden keys must be gathered before you can even touch my hilt.
Sir Prysin lost track of how to open my case in Varrock Palace.
A fortune teller in Varrock Square knows the words that wake my power.
Shadow magic later stains me black, and ancient shards turn me purple.
Wally's blade, forged to banish Delrith.
I am wielded in two hands, yet I deal no damage at all.
I first arrived as a springtime gift rather than a drop from any monster.
Diango in Draynor Village will happily hand you another if you misplace me.
My only combat option lets you whack another player harmlessly on the head.
Bwak! Dance with me and flap your arms.
I am cheap, deadly and carried into battle far more often than weapons ten times my price.
You must visit the fairy city before you are allowed to wield me.
Most adventurers smear my tip with green venom before a fight.
A quarter of your special attack bar buys two lightning-fast strikes.
Four specs in a row — the classic p++ knockout.
I am a gift from a grateful burgher on a northern isle.
I require 55 Defence and a peace won against ice trolls.
I grant both a Strength bonus and a Prayer bonus without hurting your magic or range.
A basilisk jaw transforms me into a much stronger faceguard.
White wings rise from either side of my golden brow.
Without me, certain conversations sound like little more than eerie wails.
A hermit in Lumbridge Swamp gives me away to those trying to lay a spirit to rest.
I am one of the earliest quest items new players keep in their bank for years.
Father Urhney crafted me, and the people of Port Phasmatys expect you to wear me.
Woo wooo woooo — now in plain English.
I am a strange contraption stitched together inside a haunted manor.
An undead bird, a magnet and a strip of metal keep me working.
Wear metallic chest armour and my clever trick stops working.
I snatch most of your fired arrows and bolts back into your quiver, and occasionally make steel arrows from thin air.
The green backpack every mid-level ranger wears.
The stronger my foe's arcane power, the deadlier I become.
I wait at the bottom of Mount Quidamortem for a lucky raiding party.
My power scales with the target's Magic level or Magic accuracy.
Once, a forgotten spawn outside the Farming Guild let players pick me straight off the ground.
The pale, crooked mega-rare of the Chambers of Xeric.
I never eat, never complain and never run away, though I weigh a surprising amount.
Askeladden in Rellekka hands me out to anyone willing to take care of me.
You can tell me to fetch a stick, though you will end up fetching it yourself.
Solo adventurers leave me behind on a pressure pad inside Waterbirth Island Dungeon.
You can stroke me, feed me or drop me on the floor, and I remain utterly motionless.
I slumber inside golden chests and stone sarcophagi beneath the desert sands.
Thieves searching an eight-room tomb hope to pull me out before the timer runs dry.
I can be built into an occult altar in a player's house, or recharged with ancient artefacts.
I teleport my bearer straight to Jalsavrah, Jaleustrophos and Jaldraocht.
The golden desert rod looted from Pyramid Plunder.
I look like a mechanic's tool, yet I carry a pirate's blessing.
You earn me by helping the undead crew of Braindeath Island brew a special rum.
I do not need to be equipped; simply sitting in your inventory is enough.
Carry me and every sip of a prayer potion restores a little more.
A blessed spanner that stretches your Prayer points further.
I am a relic from an era when rule-breakers were sent underground.
I am a flat, glowing ring that no longer serves my original purpose.
Long ago, Thordur sold me to prisoners who needed a way out of the Black Hole.
Nowadays I am handed out during holiday events and traded purely as a curiosity.
Spin me to revisit a vanished dwarven prison — if only I still worked.
I was meant to be a snack, yet I hit like a club.
Only a sudden visit from a travelling baker can ever place me in your hands.
Completionists dread me because no grind on earth can guarantee my drop.
I come from the Quiz Master's mystery box or a one-in-sixty-four surprise from the Sandwich Lady.
A rock-hard French loaf you can wield in your main hand.
I was forged in the desert to cut through armour that turns ordinary blades aside.
Raiders pull me from a chest guarded by the spirits of the Kharidian pantheon.
My damage never hits the very bottom or the very top of my range.
I roll accuracy twice on every stab, making high Defence almost meaningless.
The curved, dark-bladed Tombs of Amascut melee staple.
I belong to the dark son of Zamorak, deep beneath the western mountains.
You must navigate a vast, trapped cavern and cast a doll into a well to claim me.
Freshly claimed, I hold only 120 charges until a dark mage in West Ardougne upgrades me to 2,500.
I require 50 Attack and 50 Magic, and I draw power from the Well of Voyage.
Five Fire runes and a Death rune unleash my signature blast.
I live quietly by the water now, surrounded by dusty books and old memories.
Once I was a famous adventurer, though my neighbours might not approve of my retirement plan.
I can clear your bank of junk you no longer need from finished quests.
Security footage in Draynor Village shows me blowing a hole straight through a bank wall.
Dionysius himself — still wearing his stolen blue partyhat.
I have walked the same quiet loop for longer than almost anyone alive.
I rarely leave the courtyard I know so well.
Ask me nicely and I will tell you how long you have spent in this world.
I am the oldest NPC in RuneScape, greeting newcomers outside a famous castle.
I pace endlessly around Lumbridge Castle.
I am the terror that ruined an island of sailors and mages.
A guild master sends brave free-to-play heroes across the sea to end my reign.
You must patch up the Lady Lumbridge just to reach my volcanic lair.
Bring my severed head to Oziach to prove you have earned your platebody.
The green dragon of Crandor.
Thousands of hearts have raced at the mere sound of my footsteps.
I wait at the end of a long ordeal in a volcanic cavern.
Watch my feet carefully: stomp means one prayer, dangle means another.
At half health, four smaller kin crawl out to mend my wounds.
Wave 63 of the TzHaar Fight Cave.
I am one of the oldest bosses adventurers ever dared to challenge.
To reach my lair you must brave the deep Wilderness, though my cavern itself is safe from other players.
I breathe four different kinds of fire: fiery, poisonous, icy and shocking.
Pull a lever beside the Lava Maze and step into my soot-black chamber.
Three dark heads, one royal title.
I spend my days in the dark, far beneath a tidy garden.
Bring a spade to a park and you will drop straight into my tunnels.
Without a Falador hard shield to track me, you will spend half the fight chasing me in the dark.
Wyson the Gardener happily trades my claws and skins for bird nests.
Hit me below half health and I dig away across the cavern.
I am small, green and almost certainly one of the first foes you ever fought.
My kind once marched for Bandos, though now we mostly squabble over armour colours.
General Bentnoze and General Wartface argue endlessly over whether green or orange is best.
You will find plenty of us wandering east of the River Lum, dropping chef's hats and coins.
Two combat levels and a fondness for mail that fits no human.
I live for music, laughter and watching crowds scramble across the floor.
My hall once stood in Seers' Village before moving south to a white-walled city.
Pull my lever and I can summon knights to dance on the table.
Drop your treasures into my chest and I will hide them inside colourful balloons.
The balding, grinning host of the Falador Party Room.
I was cast aside by my creator as a failure, left to sleep in the frozen north.
Poke me awake after Dragon Slayer II and I will greet you with frost and venom.
Every seventh attack I unleash either a hail of acid or a crawling undead spawn.
I guard Ungael and drop the head needed to upgrade Ava's finest backpack.
The undead blue dragon known as the money printer.
The people of a misty swamp village offer sacrifices to keep me appeased.
I never stay still for long, diving beneath toxic water only to rise in a new form.
Green, red and blue — each hue demands a different combat style and prayer.
My fangs and scales forge a toxic blowpipe, a serpentine helm and a venom-laced trident.
The profit snek of Zul-Andra.
I keep to a small hut on the edge of dangerous ground.
Players have whispered my name for years, convinced I secretly control their drop luck.
I will forge a dragonfire shield from a visage for a hefty fee.
I send boastful adventurers to slay a dragon on Crandor before I will sell them my finest chestplate.
Did you remember to talk to me in Edgeville before hunting for your drop?
I am the last of an ancient dwarven order, living far from my mountain kin.
I built my small hut on a rocky southern peninsula south of Port Sarim.
I am grumpy with strangers, until a certain sweet pastry melts my heart.
I can forge a Blurite sword and award the Smithing Skillcape to masters of the anvil.
Bring me a redberry pie and I will happily talk.
I am the last surviving ourg, still fighting a war that ended an age ago.
Three loyal bodyguards — Sergeant Strongstack, Steelwill and Grimspike — fight beside me.
You must hammer a heavy door with 70 Strength just to enter my frozen stronghold.
I drop the chestplate and tassets that defined melee armour for over a decade.
For the glory of the Big High War God! Split their skulls!
I rule a vast subterranean hive beneath the Kharidian sands.
Drop two ropes into my lair — unless the Desert Elite Diary has made them permanent.
Slay my crawling first form and I burst into the air with brand-new prayers.
I was the very first boss to drop the coveted dragon chainbody.
A giant desert beetle whose second form takes wing.
I rule over a peaceful riverside town, though goblins and restless spirits still trouble my lands.
You will find me pacing the first floor of my castle, never far from my balcony.
I once entrusted a mysterious air talisman to an adventurer bound for the Wizards' Tower.
I hand out free anti-dragon shields to anyone preparing to face Elvarg.
The nobleman who governs Lumbridge.
I wore an Elysian spirit shield and a fire cape, and stood ready beside a dark cavern.
For years I assigned monsters to slayers inside the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
My cousin Steve steps in to take my post once a certain grandmaster quest concludes.
I fought beside you against Glough's demonic gorillas — and paid the ultimate price.
The beloved Slayer Master lost in Monkey Madness II.
I grew up underground, longing to see the sun-drenched surface world my people feared.
A strange mark on my forehead ties me to an ancient goblin prophecy.
I have been kidnapped by H.A.M., guided through Lumbridge and trusted with a crossbow.
I am the Chosen Commander of the peaceful Dorgeshuun tribe.
The brave cave goblin who wears a green tunic and carries a bone crossbow.
I live in a modest cottage along the northern road out of Falador.
I ask travellers for a handful of clay, copper and iron before letting them use my tools.
My task is famous for taking under ten seconds if you bring the ores with you.
Finish my little errand and my pair of anvils are yours to hammer forever.
The dwarf whose quest is the shortest in all of Gielinor.
I guard the river of souls deep beneath Taverley Dungeon.
You need 91 Slayer and a hellhound task just to step past the flames into my lair.
When I howl 'Arooooo!', three ghostly figures march forward to drain your Prayer.
I drop primordial, pegasian and eternal crystals to upgrade your boots.
The three-headed hellhound of the underworld.
I am a vast, pale creature that slumbers in the deepest cavern of Mount Quidamortem.
My left claw and right claw must be crippled together before my head can be felled.
I breathe crystal spikes, falling rocks, acid trails and swirling teleport portals.
Solo raiders learn to run left and right across my room in a four-tick rhythm.
The final boss of the Chambers of Xeric.
I haunt a barren cavern in the Wilderness, though no player-killer can reach you inside my chamber.
Most weapons deal only half their damage to me — bring a spear or halberd instead.
A leaping Dark Energy Core drains your life to heal me unless you stun or trap it.
My rarest drops are the arcane, spectral and elysian sigils.
A colossal, spectral hound of 2,000 hitpoints.
I sit upon a grand throne, applauding as mortals bleed for my entertainment.
I rule over the vampyric nobility of Ver Sinhaza in Morytania.
First you must shatter my shield with the Dawnbringer, then survive my webs, yellow pools and purple tornadoes.
In my final phase I shed my regal form and skitter across the arena as a monstrous spider.
The Lady of the Theatre of Blood.
I am a towering beast locked inside the lowest tier of Mount Karuulm.
Only Konar quo Maten can assign you the task needed to enter my chamber at 95 Slayer.
Lure me over red, green and blue chemical vents to weaken my scales.
Count my attacks in threes: poison, lightning, fire, and finally jad-like fury.
My claw forges the dragon hunter lance, and my leather becomes ferocious gloves.
I rule a flourishing woodland kingdom from the base of a colossal tree.
My trusted advisor Glough has caused me no end of trouble and betrayal.
I send adventurers across the sea to Ape Atoll and out to stop a corrupted battleship.
Find me on the ground floor of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
The royal gnome monarch with a crown upon his head.
Almost every legend in Gielinor began its very first step upon my cobblestones.
A gentle river splits my castle from fields of goblins, cows and chickens.
A frantic cook in my kitchen is always short an egg, a pot of flour and a bucket of milk.
Fall in battle anywhere in the world and, by default, you wake up in my courtyard.
Home to Duke Horacio, Bob's Brilliant Axes and a world-famous starter castle.
My bright white walls and manicured park make me the tidiest city in Asgarnia.
An order of pun-named knights governs my castle while dwarves tunnel beneath my eastern quarter.
On 6 June 2006, a famous glitch turned my peaceful streets into a massacre.
Party Pete hosts drop parties in my south-east corner, and Wyson tends the park.
The white-walled city of the White Knights.
Warm desert winds sweep through my sandstone streets just east of the River Lum.
For years, travellers had to pay ten coins at my western gate unless they had rescued a prince.
Silk merchants, kebab sellers and a palace full of warriors crowd my bazaar.
Shantay guards the pass to the south, and a glider lands upon my northern cliffs.
The desert emirate east of Lumbridge.
Every adventurer knows my shores, yet once you leave, you can never return.
You will bake your first bread, smith your first bronze dagger and slay your first giant rat here.
Vannaka, Brother Brace and the Survival Expert each teach you a piece of the trade.
A final spell cast upon a chicken sends you on your way to the mainland.
Where Gielinor Guide greets brand-new accounts.
I am a quiet, shadowed settlement tucked between Lumbridge and Port Sarim.
A dark manor looms to my north, and a haunted jail sits just to my east.
My marketplace offers seeds, dye, toys and a bank with a hole once blasted in its wall.
Aggie the witch, Ned the rope-maker and the Wise Old Man all live within a stone's throw.
Woodcutters chop willow trees along my southern shore, watched by dark wizards.
A tall stone wall splits my sprawling capital in two.
On one side, merchants hawk silk and cake around a bustling square; on the other, mourners guard a supposed plague.
Thieves have spent countless hours picking pockets and lifting cakes in my market.
King Lathas rules my eastern half, while a zoo and a monastery lie near my borders.
The divided capital of Kandarin.
The smell of salt air, tar and fresh fish hangs over my wooden piers.
Sailors gather at the Rusty Anchor while prisoners rattle the bars of my jail.
From my docks you can sail to Karamja, Entrana, Pest Control and Great Kourend.
A famous sea shanty plays the moment you stroll down my jetties.
Asgarnia's busiest harbour — home to Sea Shanty 2.
No sun ever warms my grey cobblestones, and my townsfolk hide a hairy secret.
Cross the River Salve and follow the swamp road north to find my gates.
My rooftops are one of the most popular places in Gielinor to gather Marks of Grace.
Mazchna assigns Slayer tasks here, and the Hair of the Dog tavern pours a grim pint.
The werewolf town of Morytania.
I am a peaceful sanctuary where violence is forbidden by holy law.
Monks inspect your pockets on the dock before letting you board the ship to my shore.
No weapons or armour may cross my waters — though raw materials and unstrung bows slip right past.
The Law Altar stands upon my grass, and a dangerous cavern hides beneath my church.
The sacred Saradominist island west of Port Sarim.
You will not find me on the world map, yet thousands of travellers pass through me every day.
A humble shed in Lumbridge Swamp hides the doorway to my glowing streets.
My wheat fields shimmer with crop circles, and my choir sings beside a cosmic altar.
Chaeldar assigns tasks here, and a fairy ring hub sits at my heart.
The hidden fairy city upon Gielinor's moon.
For generations I existed only as a seed, hidden behind a wall of mist and mountains.
Eight elven clans share my gleaming spires and gardens.
Complete Song of the Elves and my gates finally open to you.
Zalcano's prison, the Gauntlet and a singing bowl for crystal gear all lie within my walls.
The ancient crystal city of Tirannwn.
I stand at the southernmost edge of a scorching desert, scarred by plague and jackals.
A high wall separates me from my grander sister city across the river.
Deep beneath my streets lie a temple of Icthlarin, a Slayer dungeon and a pyramid full of traps.
Thieves plunder my grandest tomb in search of a golden sceptre.
Look around, traveller — I am the very city where the Sphinx awaits.
